a low-communication and high-performance data-parallel implementation of the EverGlades Landscape Fire Model was successfully developed in a network of Workstations.
the MPI parallel implementation of the ELFM code is a high-performance data parallel algorithm.
the performance of the ELFM using MPI was enhanced by using the rollback and checkpointing mechanisms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and implementation of a parallel algorithm for the Everglades fire modeling problem using MPI on NOWs.
the development of a parallel version of ELFM that will run on a network of work-stations.
the design and implementation of a parallel implementation of the ELFM in a network of workstation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the parallel implementation of the ELFM using MPI and the checkpointing and the rollback techniques is a promising alternative to the serial implementation of ELFM.
the parallel implementation of the ELFM using MPI and checkpointing is an efficient and effective approach to solving the problem.
the parallel ELFM program using MPI and checkpointing is efficient and scalable.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the parallel implementation of ELFM using checkpointing and rollback techniques in MPI on NOWs is a viable approach to solving the problem of fire propagation.
the performance of the parallel ELFM is significantly enhanced by the checkpointing and rolling back mechanisms.
the parallel implementation of ELFM in NOWs is feasible and efficient.
The main takeaway from our work is that
MPI is a good choice to implement a parallel model that has a dynamic component and irregular data access pattern.
the parallel implementation of the ELFM model is a viable option for large scale fire modeling in a network of heterogeneous workstations.
the use of MPI in conjunction with checkpointing and rollback techniques can be used to develop high performance parallel codes for irregular applications.
